transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-03-04 10:00 PST | Duration: ~45m
Attendees: Evan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Jonah (CSM), Lina (SE), Dr Lisa Chen (Sapphire), Aaron Patel (Sapphire), Maya Ortiz (Sapphire), Tom Nguyen (Sapphire Security)

00:00 Evan: hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate the time. quick intros, then priya will walk through the quality results from last week's run.
00:12 Dr. Lisa: thanks, Evan. hi all.
00:15 Priya: ok so quick TLDR, we ran the 2k clinician prompt set against three model/config variants - hosted redwood-base-002 (open quant), dedicated-gn5-16q, and a fallback smaller quant model. We measured accuracy, hallucination rate, and clinically-relevant precision on the diagnosis extraction task.
00:40 Aaron: when you say hallucination rate can you define? like false facts vs made-up meds?
00:47 Priya: good point, yeah we split hallucination into two buckets: factual fabrications (wrong dates, wrong diagnosis) and extraneous medication suggestions (stuff not in the record). scoring uses fuzzy string match + clinical ontology mapping so it's not just token overlap.
01:10 Maya: initial reading looks positive but we saw the redwood-base-002 spike on hallucinations for long context prompts.
01:18 Priya: yes that's correct - when prompts exceed ~1.2k tokens we saw KV-cache thrash and more off-topic completions. dedicated config with a larger sequence kernel handled it better.
01:35 Tom: quick security note, any of those runs touched PHI in the hosted environment? we need confirmation of no persistent storage and encryption in transit/rest.
01:45 Evan: all runs used anonymized test data; no PHI persisted. but we will send the security pack that details retention, KMS integration, and audit logs.
01:55 Dr. Lisa: perfect, please include the SOC 2 and your KMS flow.
02:03 Priya: onto the numbers - overall accuracy on diagnosis extraction: hosted ~78%, dedicated ~86%, fallback model ~70%. Hallucination rate: hosted 9.2%, dedicated 4.7%, fallback 14%. Latency (median token latency) hosted ~65ms per token, dedicated ~48ms per token. p95 latency hosted hit 320ms on long contexts.
02:32 Aaron: ok those dedicated numbers look promising. what's the cost delta?
02:36 Evan: we estimated dedicated pilot nodes at roughly 2.3x per-token cost vs hosted baseline but you get capacity guarantees and lower p95 tails. we can send a detailed price sheet.
02:48 Maya: regarding guardrails - we saw two near-miss cases where the model returned a specific med name that was obfuscated in prompt. are those failures flagged in the eval?
02:58 Priya: we have a guardrail scorer that checks for named-entity leakage and PHI patterns; both near-miss cases were scored as warnings but not hard failures because the model redacted on follow-up. That said, we agree we should tighten the threshold and add a rule to always redact certain token categories.
03:20 Dr. Lisa: we need deterministic redaction, can't rely on follow-up redaction. so a hard stop if med names are inferred.
03:27 Priya: understood; action item - add deterministic redaction rule to pipeline and re-run the 2k set.
03:33 Jonah: and record that as regression test so it doesn't slip in later rollouts.
03:38 Aaron: another datapoint, we saw model reasoning degrade on prompts with nested lists - bullet lists of symptoms confuse it sometimes, it merges entries. is that a model thing or prompt engineer thing?
03:50 Lina: usually it's a mix. we found adding explicit separators and a short instruction "preserve list items" improved structure output. also temperature scheduling and nucleus sampling adjustments helped. We recommend a small prompt rewrite and a post-processing reranker for list structure.
04:10 Maya: can Redwood run a prompt reformat pass automatically or we need to give the rewrites?
04:15 Priya: we can run a preprocessor that normalizes input to canonical list format as part of the inference pipeline; we will prototype that in the next regression run.
04:23 Tom: on encryption - our security team needs HSM/KMS diagram and proof that KMS keys are customer-controlled for private deployments. Hosted won't fly unless keys are customer-managed.
04:34 Evan: we'll include the KMS/HSM details in the pack. for hosted options we support customer-managed keys via our KMS integration and BYOK flow, but for true key custody you may prefer private deployment.
04:47 Dr. Lisa: timeline question - if we tighten guardrails and re-run a full regression suite, how long until we get results?
04:52 Priya: the big run (10k prompts) takes about 48h on the reserved dedicated nodes. smaller 2k runs are 3-4 hours. we'll queue a 10k run on dedicated config once Aaron sends the additional clinician prompts they promised.
05:08 Aaron: yep I'll upload the extra cases today/tomorrow. I also want a CSV of failure examples so we can triage.
05:14 Priya: we'll export a failure CSV with context, model output, score, and rule that failed.
05:21 Evan: item - we'll also attach sample audio highlights and the brief demo video of the reranker behavior.
05:28 Maya: on metrics - can Redwood also surface a per-prompt confidence score that our triage UI can use?
05:33 Lina: yes, we emit a calibrated confidence score and embedding similarity score; you can threshold it at the UI layer or have server-side blocking.
05:43 Dr. Lisa: great. can that score be auditable in logs for compliance?
05:47 Evan: yes audit logs include model version, prompt hash, confidence score, and routing decision. we'll show a log sample in the security pack.
05:55 Aaron: question about regression - if we pin model version and push guardrail rules, how do we handle automatic fallback if a newer model regresses?
06:04 Priya: we recommend a canary plus automated regression check: new model version runs against your benchmark set; if it fails threshold we route to a fallback variant automatically. Redwood console can manage rollouts.
06:18 Maya: will the console show token-level cost breakdown per route?
06:22 Evan: yes, per-route token cost, median/p95 latency, and failure counts.
06:27 Tom: legal/procurement wanted to know what evidence is needed to go to a pilot contract - security pack + SLA and sample indemnity clauses.
06:35 Evan: we'll push a pilot addendum and sample SLA with turnaround.
06:40 Dr. Lisa: ok can we recap next steps?
06:43 Evan: sure - priya will run the regression suite on dedicated with tightened redaction rules and preprocessor for lists; upload benchmark CSVs and failure CSV. Priya due 2026-03-10. Aaron will upload 200 additional clinician prompts and failure priority list by 2026-03-08. Evan will send security pack and pricing by 2026-03-06. Tom will confirm KMS requirements by 2026-03-09. we'll schedule the dedicated throughput benchmark for week of 2026-03-16.
07:15 Dr. Lisa: that covers it, thanks everyone.
07:18 Evan: thanks all, we'll follow up in email with links - security pack link: https://redwood.example.com/security/sapphire-poc-pack (note: placeholder). benchmark spreadsheet link: https://redwood.example.com/benchmarks/sapphire-pilot (placeholder).
07:32 Aaron: thanks. bye.

End of transcript.

Notes on transcription quality: automatic transcript with occasional speaker mismatch and small mis-words (e.g., "KV cash" instead of "KV cache"). Some technical terms spelled differently in customer notes.

References shared: security pack (link above), benchmark spreadsheet (link above), sample reranker demo video (link provided via email).

Recap (short): dedicated config reduces hallucinations and p95 latency; customer mandates deterministic PHI redaction; Redwood to run extended regression and share security/pricing artifacts.
